grh_43972dc08c5cbc7def2d.title: Dont Look Down
paragraphs: While attending a medical meeting in New York, Dr. Christian is asked to help Joe Lance, a discouraged veteran who has reached a crisis after years of feeling trapped by a dull job, a troubled marriage and responsibility for his younger sister Audrey. Christian spends hours talking with Joe and gradually learns that beneath the despair he still wants the ordinary things he believes life has denied him: a real home, children, companionship and even simple pleasures such as fishing. Audrey's engagement removes one burden, but initially makes Joe feel even less needed. Christian refuses to deceive him and instead persuades the police to honor a promise allowing Joe time to reconsider. Joe finally comes back inside. His wife Emma, confronted with how selfish and distant their marriage has become, takes a risk of her own to reach him emotionally and promises that they will build the home and family he has wanted. Joe chooses to return with her. Audrey and Tim also prepare to marry, and Christian leaves New York with the family reconciled and looking forward rather than giving up.

grh_438a6c1fc9b68a3ee48d.title: Thicker Than Water
paragraphs: Britt meets wandering gambler Gus Proctor, who is returning after years away to a family he barely knows, only to learn that his wife Janet has died and their son Ted is being raised by Janet's sister Amy. Ted quickly idolizes the glamorous father he had been told was dead and decides to run away with Gus and become a gambler himself. Realizing what his example is doing, Gus deliberately lets himself be exposed as a poker cheat so the boy will reject that life and stay with Amy. Ted abandons the plan to run away, while Amy later marries the dependable Fred Baker, who becomes a steady father figure to him.

grh_4322daebd8666e3aefdc.title: Much To Do About Marty
paragraphs: Laurie Gary separates from her bandleader husband Marty after years of having their private life turned into material for his jokes, while Marty resents Laurie's increasingly determined effort to make him quieter, more dignified and socially conventional. Dr. Christian compares them to children in a tug of war and suggests that Marty stop pulling back for a while. Marty therefore gives Laurie exactly the refined husband she says she wants, trading his usual gags and show-business energy for quiet evenings, classical reading and restraint. The experiment makes both of them see what they have been demanding from the other. After Laurie gets a closer look at how difficult Marty's comic work really is, Marty promises not to exploit everything she says for a gag, and Laurie promises not to be so sensitive about the humor that is part of him. They reconcile without either having to become someone else.

grh_43b8e51f16fdcbb97453.title: Unfinished Business
paragraphs: Benjamin Stack has organized every minute of his marriage into a rigid schedule until his wife Maddie finally leaves, saying she has lived with a system instead of a man. Dr. Christian tries to help them reconcile, but even when Maddie asks only for spontaneity, Benjamin immediately tries to turn their life together into a modified timetable. After losing her again, his ordered world collapses so completely that he prepares to jump from a building. Dr. Christian talks him down by appealing to the one thing Benjamin still cannot abandon: an unpaid obligation, inventing a large medical bill that must be settled first. With the immediate crisis over, Dr. Christian recommends an unplanned road trip with Maddie, although Benjamin's first instinct is still to schedule every mile and meal.

grh_43a38935a43a2594f6b3.title: Lost Island
paragraphs: Army engineer Major George Dodd arrives on a peaceful South Pacific island to prepare it for conversion into an American airbase. As he grows close to Ruth, Vigo, Father Vincent and the island community, he realizes the runways and military facilities will erase homes, gardens, sacred meeting places and even Vigo's turtle nesting ground. The islanders initially welcome the arriving ship because they do not understand what it means. Dodd is devastated by the destruction but accepts the base as part of defeating fascism, and he and Ruth remain to help the displaced people endure the loss while the new airfield rises.
